completion_data.completion_summary: Phase 3 of plan v5 implemented: proved flo_limit (FLO maintained at limit stages) fully sorry-free. FLO's own FLO-1/FLO-2 conclusions are stage-independent on the RHS (statements purely about the FloSeq/rankOf/predecessor-stage membership), so membership/relatedness at a limit stage descends directly through FloSeq.limit_eq's raw Set.iUnion/existential union to a witnessing predecessor stage tau < sigma, and FLO at that smaller stage (from the phase's own hflo hypothesis) closes the goal for sigma unchanged -- no dependence on FloSeq.mono or ChainCtx.unionContext/chain_closure was needed, a documented Plan Deviation from the task list's suggested route. Zero-debt invariant holds; primeLemma's axiom footprint unchanged in kind (no new axiom); probe sorry count dropped from 6 to 5.

memory_candidates.content: When an invariant predicate P is stated relative to a construction-stage index sigma but its own clauses only mention sigma on the LHS (membership/relatedness AT sigma) while the RHS conclusion is phrased purely in terms of the underlying object (e.g. a globally-defined rank/sInf function) -- proving P is preserved at a LIMIT stage of a stage-indexed transfinite construction can often skip monotonicity/union-identification machinery entirely: just descend, via the raw-union defining equation, to ANY witnessing predecessor stage tau < sigma where the LHS already holds, and invoke P at tau directly, since its RHS conclusion is sigma-independent and transfers verbatim. Check for this shape before reaching for ChainCtx-style abstractions.
